decisions.reason: As a core, close-to-existing camera product that kept its own page in both 2023 and 2024, it likely meets continuation aspirations and uses capabilities the firm already has.

This modular navigation camera is a multi-model line in the firm's core business and remained prominently presented, so management would likely see enough strategic and commercial promise to retain it.
The sensor suite extends the established offer and still had its own page in 2024, indicating acceptable performance or at least sufficient promise to stay above the drop threshold.
Its lower website prominence suggests weaker current traction, but it fits the firm's push toward miniaturized space sensors and a large established firm would usually give such a product more time.

A newly launched radiation-hard camera line with its own page is highly aligned with the firm's heritage, and behavioral-theory logic implies strong tolerance for early uncertainty in such a core area.

The asteroid navigation camera is niche and only mentioned on the website, so aspiration shortfall risk is higher, but its exploratory value and fit with mission-imaging capabilities make continuation still slightly more likely than withdrawal.
